verdicts.quote: Use a Lightning Web Component in an explicitly deployed Custom Tab … Send ordered text inputs with user and assistant roles from the current view. There is no trusted Salesforce record context in the request.
No Salesforce business-record read or write is in scope, so record sharing, object CRUD and field permissions are inapplicable to chat data access.
verdicts.missing: The bot preserves visibility by excluding records. The spec gives no rule for answering from records under the asking user’s sharing context.

verdicts.quote: No Salesforce business-record read or write is in scope, so record sharing, object CRUD and field permissions are inapplicable to chat data access.
verdicts.missing: The spec excludes all business-record fields. It gives no field-level access or masking rule for reading or displaying encrypted or restricted fields.

verdicts.quote: The explicitly granted user can invoke the bot. … Use additive metadata and scoped permission sets for access. … the integration administrator can rotate or revoke the key through approved administrative channels.
Only that view's current user reads the rendered copy. … Names, prompt/response text, secrets, raw provider bodies and headers stay out of app-owned telemetry
Use an imperative, non-cacheable Lightning-to-Apex request for each accepted send. … A server transaction allows one inference callout per send.
verdicts.missing: The spec calls xAI from the send transaction. It specifies neither asynchronous Apex execution nor the restrictions on trigger invocation and callouts following DML.

verdicts.quote: Use an enhanced Salesforce Named Credential over HTTPS with a Custom External Credential … Provision the secret separately via authorized admin setup … No provider credential in product source, browser artifacts, chat display, app-owned logs or handoff.
Salesforce documents a maximum of 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative callout time per transaction, and a synchronous maximum request or response size of 6 MB with heap use also accounted for.
verdicts.missing: The numeric Apex heap and CPU-time ceilings are unspecified. The 6 MB figure bounds request or response size.

verdicts.quote: Controlled delayed, distinct successes and failure fixtures verify displayed text, status, submitted prompts and call count.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open how Apex tests substitute mock responses for live callouts. It names neither the live-callout restriction nor the required mock implementation.

Use an imperative, non-cacheable Lightning-to-Apex request for each accepted send. … When the latest active request returns a completed nonempty reply, commit the pair once and announce completion.

verdicts.where: AD-3, R-2 D; R-2 D/R-3 B walkthrough
verdicts.quote: Identify sends with a view generation and operation identity. … Ignore late or duplicate completion after settlement … T-4 invalidated the first operation, so the two outbound calls produce exactly one pair

verdicts.where: AD-2, R-2 state and service contract
verdicts.quote: verify the target's concurrent-callout limit … No cached replies, durable queue, provider continuity ID, subscription, cursor or incremental synchronization.
verdicts.missing: The spec addresses concurrency for direct calls. It defines neither a job capacity nor the outcome of a failed enqueue.

verdicts.quote: show an actionable, sanitized message. … Check credential failure, 429, 5xx, network failure, timeout, invalid body and incomplete/empty output. … A missing, disabled or rejected credential produces an actionable setup error
verdicts.missing: Credential rejection has a setup error. The messages or recovery actions that distinguish other 4xx refusals, 5xx failures and timeouts for the user are unspecified.

verdicts.where: R-2 C, R-2 B–C/R-3 A walkthrough
verdicts.quote: No automatic retry or duplicate send while pending. … Send P2 with a 429: the second outbound attempt ends under T-4, leaving one pair and draft P2.
verdicts.missing: Retry is manual. The spec leaves open what the rate-limit or quota message tells the user about when to retry or when quota needs administrative attention.

verdicts.where: R-2 C, R-2 B–C/R-3 A walkthrough
verdicts.quote: timeout or malformed/incomplete result, remove pending state, keep prior pairs, restore the draft and show an actionable, sanitized message. … No partial text appears.
Keep drafts, completed turns, appearance selection and pending state in the current component's memory. … Send ordered text inputs with user and assistant roles from the current view.
verdicts.missing: The view holds turns, roles, text and status in memory. No conversation or turn record schema specifies timestamps, per-turn model identity or usage counts.

verdicts.where: R-3 B, R-4 state and data assessment
verdicts.quote: Leaving the chat, refresh, sign-out or identity change ends that view's state. … xAI documents default audit retention of 30 days and a team-level zero-data-retention option
verdicts.missing: The spec describes local chat lifetime and provider retention. It leaves the effect of deleting a Salesforce user on an open chat or a provider-held copy unspecified.

verdicts.quote: tells users to use synthetic/non-sensitive text … No Salesforce record lookup, Salesforce user identifiers or attachments in the inference payload. … Send ordered text inputs with user and assistant roles from the current view.
Do not silently clip user input or retained context. … A context-limit rejection lets the user clear chat or shorten the draft where that fits the budget.
verdicts.missing: Oversized context is rejected intact. The model-specific size limit and counting rule remain open.

verdicts.quote: A fresh view begins with no prior context. … Empty, whitespace-only or over-budget input starts no provider call. … Accept exactly the configured limit under a documented counting rule and reject the first value above it.

verdicts.where: R-1 state and service contract, R-4 state and data assessment, R-4 C
verdicts.quote: the responsible admin withdraws bot access … The integration administrator owns the secret and non-secret route/model configuration … Authorized operators can distinguish successful completion, provider rejection by safe category, timeout and invalid response

verdicts.where: R-4 state and data assessment, R-1 C
verdicts.quote: route/model configuration scoped to this bot and target org. … Provision separately from deployable configuration. … Release operators confirm the candidate reached terminal success, read back the candidate and authorized configuration
verdicts.missing: The spec scopes configuration and secret provisioning to the development org and verifies deployment. It leaves scratch-org versus sandbox selection, cross-environment promotion and production code coverage unspecified.

verdicts.where: R-2 C, non-functional requirements for R-2 and R-3
verdicts.quote: Show the pending message and an accessible progress status as soon as a valid send starts. … A finite wait ends in success or recoverable failure, including a lost connection.
verdicts.missing: The wait must end, but the spec gives no elapsed-time target or numeric upper bound for the user to receive an answer or timeout.
